repo_model.summary: Root main.py is a RelBench candidate that loads a task from the sanitized cache and writes NumPy validation/test predictions. The supplied implementation is a task-family baseline, while kapso_evaluation executes candidates and scores official validation metrics.

entrypoints.how_to_run: From the repository root, run python main.py --debug for the cheap pipeline check or python main.py for the full run.
Run python kapso_evaluation/grader.py --fidelity fast|full [--fraction F] [--seed S] with the required RelBench environment variables.

where_to_edit.role: Primary candidate implementation and root entrypoint; replace the trivial prediction logic here.
Optional task-loading, prediction-saving, temporal-safety, and MAP@K helpers.
Evaluation contract defining output files, alignment, data access, and prediction formats.
Local pre-validation tool for prediction shapes, dtypes, finiteness, and binary ranges.
Immutable official evaluator; candidate changes should not reimplement or modify it.

claims.statement: main.py is the end-to-end candidate pipeline: it reads the dataset/task identity from environment variables, loads the RelBench task without downloading, determines split sizes, detects zero-validation-row rolling snapshots, and writes prediction arrays to the run data directory.

evidence.description: Sets the validation row count based on the cached val table.
Writes validation predictions for non-rolling runs.

claims.statement: The supplied baseline branches by task family: recommendations emit tiled ranked IDs 0 through eval_k-1, binary classification emits 0.5 probabilities, multiclass classification emits uniform class scores, and all other tasks emit the training target median.
kapso_datasets.common.load_task constructs a TaskContext containing the dataset, task, database, and train/validation/test tables, while save_predictions centralizes writing both prediction files.

evidence.description: Obtains the database with the configured timestamp cutoff.
Loads the train, validation, and test tables.

claims.statement: kapso_evaluation/grader.py runs main.py as an isolated subprocess with fidelity-specific timeouts, validates the resulting files, computes official RelBench validation metrics, and archives full-fidelity runs.

evidence.description: Selects main.py or main.py --debug by fidelity.
Computes task evaluation metrics on validation predictions.

claims.statement: With a rolling root, the grader invokes the candidate once per snapshot, collects each tick's test predictions, and assembles final vectors according to the snapshot indices.

evidence.description: Checks per-tick prediction length against snapshot indices.

claims.statement: The supplied main.py requires RELBENCH_DATASET, RELBENCH_TASK, RELBENCH_CACHE_DIR, and KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR to be present in its environment.

evidence.description: Reads the required run output directory.

claims.statement: Every ordinary run must produce val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy with rows positionally aligned to the task validation and test tables; validation predictions must be out-of-sample and cannot be trained on validation labels.

evidence.description: Requires both prediction files after every run.
Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample.

claims.statement: Prediction formats are task-specific: binary and regression use float vectors, multiclass uses an (N,C) float array, and recommendation uses an (N,K) integer array of distinct valid destination IDs.

evidence.description: Defines binary and regression formats and ranges.

claims.statement: The standard TaskContext treats train and validation as labeled tables, while test contains only seed IDs and timestamps; test labels are absent from the sanitized cache.

evidence.description: Documents test seed IDs and timestamps only.
States that test labels are physically absent.

claims.statement: The search score of record is the official primary validation metric; test metrics are private and are not available during the search loop.

evidence.description: Defines the official validation primary metric as the search score.
States that test metrics are computed privately.
Places the selected validation metric in the manifest score.

claims.statement: The fastest end-to-end sanity check is python main.py --debug; the harness also runs python main.py for the full training path.

evidence.description: States that the harness runs the program twice.

claims.statement: After writing predictions, python kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py validates file presence, expected shapes, recommendation integer types and ranges, finite values, and binary probability bounds.

evidence.description: Checks both validation and test splits.

claims.statement: A successful official evaluation prints OFFICIAL VALIDATION METRICS and a KAPSO_EVAL_MANIFEST line containing the primary validation score; full-fidelity runs additionally report an archive name.

evidence.description: Stores the primary metric as manifest score.

claims.statement: Rolling detection is based on n_val == 0, including snapshots with an empty or absent val.parquet; in that mode the supplied main.py intentionally writes only test_predictions.npy per tick, while the grader assembles final validation and test vectors.

evidence.description: Documents empty validation tables in rolling snapshots.
Sets n_val to zero when the validation cache file is absent.
Derives rolling mode from zero validation rows.
Suppresses validation output in rolling mode.
Writes assembled split vectors after rolling execution.

claims.statement: The baseline recommendation row ignores num_dst_nodes and emits IDs 0 through eval_k-1; if eval_k exceeds the destination range, the checker only warns about out-of-range IDs, so a real recommender must enforce the destination-ID contract itself.

evidence.description: Constructs recommendation IDs solely from eval_k.
Requires recommendation IDs to be valid destination IDs.
Warns rather than failing for out-of-range IDs.

claims.statement: For autocomplete tasks, load_task defaults to a database cut off at the test timestamp; pass upto_test_timestamp=False when post-test-cutoff entity rows are needed as inputs.
Evaluation processes must be run in the foreground: the session terminates and kills processes when the response ends, so backgrounded evaluations will not complete or score.
The candidate depends on NumPy and RelBench, specifically RelBench task/base APIs and NumPy array persistence.

evidence.description: States that Python with relbench and numpy is sufficient.

claims.statement: The evaluation handler supplies task identity, primary metric, archive/work directories, timeouts, the sanitized RelBench cache, and a shared cross-experiment cache through environment variables.

evidence.description: Lists metric, work directory, and timeout variables.

claims.statement: Data access must use the sanitized read-only cache with download=False; the supplied loader obtains both the dataset and task without attempting network downloads.

evidence.description: Requires RelBench API access with download=False.
